task_3.title: Support pytest CLI argument files via @path
task_3.description: Pytest 8.2.0 adds support for loading command-line arguments from a text file by passing an argument prefixed with `@`. This makes large invocations easier to manage while preserving normal CLI parsing semantics for the loaded arguments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest accepts a text file of command-line arguments when the invocation includes an `@`-prefixed path, so users can supply long lists of test targets and other CLI arguments without expanding them directly in the shell.

expectation.grounded: The pytest command-line interface should accept `@<file>` as an input token and read additional arguments from that file. Each line in the file should be treated as one command-line argument, and the resulting arguments should be parsed by pytest through the normal option and `file_or_dir` handling flow exactly as if they had been provided directly on the command line.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to place a pytest invocation's arguments in a plain text file and run pytest by referencing that file with `@...`. Pytest should behave the same as if those arguments had been typed directly into the terminal.

constraints.grounded: The feature should use `@`-prefixed argument-file expansion rather than introducing a separate dedicated flag. Argument files are line-oriented: one argument per line. Existing direct CLI usage without `@<file>` must continue to parse and execute normally.
constraints.conceptual: This should extend the existing CLI rather than replace it. The new input form must remain compatible with current command usage and should require a simple text file format where each line represents one argument.

behavior: An `@`-prefixed command-line token is interpreted as a reference to a file containing additional pytest arguments.
Each newline-delimited entry in the referenced file is expanded into a separate argument before normal pytest command-line parsing continues.
Arguments loaded from the file participate in standard pytest parsing, so positional test selections and regular CLI options behave the same as when passed directly.
The feature improves readability and maintainability of long pytest invocations without changing the behavior of existing non-argfile invocations.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs pytest with `@path/to/args.txt`, pytest should load the referenced file and treat each line as a separate CLI argument.
When the argument file contains multiple test paths or node IDs, pytest should select and run those targets as though they had been passed directly on the command line.
When the argument file contains standard pytest options together with test targets, pytest should honor those options in the same invocation.
When pytest is run without any `@`-prefixed argument file, existing command-line behavior should remain unchanged.

task_2.title: Adopt pathlib-based pytest hook parameters
task_2.description: Pytest 8.2.0 now emits deprecation warnings for plugin hook implementations that still declare legacy py.path.local-based hook parameters. Update hook signatures to the pathlib.Path-based parameter names introduced earlier so plugins remain warning-free on 8.2.0 and compatible before the legacy arguments are removed in pytest 9.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that plugin hook implementations no longer rely on deprecated legacy path-hook arguments and remain warning-free under pytest 8.2.0 by using the current pathlib-based parameters for collection and reporting hooks.

expectation.grounded: Hook implementations for `pytest_ignore_collect`, `pytest_collect_file`, and `pytest_pycollect_makemodule` should declare the pathlib-based parameters `collection_path`, `file_path`, and `module_path` instead of the deprecated `path` argument. Hook implementations for `pytest_report_header` and `pytest_report_collectionfinish` should declare `start_path` instead of the deprecated `startdir` argument. Under pytest 8.2.0, implementations that still request these legacy arguments should be treated as deprecated and emit a deprecation warning.
expectation.conceptual: Plugins should use the modern path parameters exposed by pytest hooks so collection and reporting integrations work without deprecation warnings in pytest 8.2.0 and stay compatible with the planned removal of legacy path arguments.

constraints.grounded: Preserve each hook's existing observable behavior aside from the deprecation state of its signature. The update should only replace deprecated hook argument names with their current pathlib-based equivalents and must not change the hook being implemented, its return contract, or the semantics of collection and report customization.
constraints.conceptual: Keep plugin behavior the same for end users. The only intended change is that supported hook signatures use current path inputs and no longer depend on deprecated legacy-path arguments.

behavior: Implementations of `pytest_ignore_collect` that declare `path` are now deprecated; the supported path argument is `collection_path`.
Implementations of `pytest_collect_file` that declare `path` are now deprecated; the supported path argument is `file_path`.
Implementations of `pytest_pycollect_makemodule` that declare `path` are now deprecated; the supported path argument is `module_path`.
Implementations of `pytest_report_header` that declare `startdir` are now deprecated; the supported path argument is `start_path`.
Implementations of `pytest_report_collectionfinish` that declare `startdir` are now deprecated; the supported path argument is `start_path`.
When pytest encounters hook implementations using these legacy parameters, it now emits a deprecation warning instead of remaining silent.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin implements `pytest_ignore_collect`, `pytest_collect_file`, or `pytest_pycollect_makemodule`, it should accept the corresponding pathlib-based parameter name and should not rely on the deprecated `path` argument.
When a plugin implements `pytest_report_header` or `pytest_report_collectionfinish`, it should accept `start_path` and should not rely on the deprecated `startdir` argument.
When the plugin is loaded under pytest 8.2.0, supported hook implementations should not trigger deprecation warnings related to legacy path-hook arguments.
Collection and reporting customizations should continue to produce the same user-visible outcomes after the signature update.

task_1.title: Align pytest unittest collection with bound-instance semantics
task_1.description: Pytest 8.2.0 changes how unittest-based tests are collected and represented. Collection now creates a temporary TestCase instance using the placeholder method name runTest, and unittest test items now behave more like regular class-based pytest items by exposing bound methods and instance-aware fixture resolution. This improves consistency, but custom TestCase subclasses that cannot be instantiated with runTest may now fail during collection.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.2.0 preserves unittest-based test collection and execution by supporting collection-time instantiation with runTest and by treating collected TestCase methods as instance-bound tests with consistent fixture behavior.

expectation.grounded: Pytest's unittest integration should instantiate unittest.TestCase subclasses as MyTestCase("runTest") when it needs a temporary instance for collection and fixture discovery. TestCaseFunction.obj should behave like other class-based pytest items by resolving against a bound method on an instance, and FixtureRequest.instance should expose that instance only for function-scoped requests. Fixtures defined as methods should bind against the active request.instance without a separate unittest-only calling path. Custom TestCase subclasses that override __init__ must not fail when the method name is runTest.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, unittest-style tests should behave like normal class-based pytest tests from the user's perspective: pytest should work with a real test instance during collection, method-based fixtures should see the current test object, and custom TestCase subclasses should remain collectable as long as they tolerate the placeholder runTest method name used during discovery.

constraints.grounded: Do not expose a TestCase instance for non-function fixture scopes. Do not require special-case unittest fixture argument discovery separate from the standard bound-method path. Preserve unittest-driven execution for async test methods and normal setUp/tearDown behavior while using the collected instance. Treat inability to instantiate a TestCase with runTest as a collection-time compatibility failure rather than silently skipping the class.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must keep unittest execution semantics intact while tightening collection requirements. Instance-specific behavior should only exist where a real test instance is meaningful, and unsupported constructor patterns should fail explicitly during collection instead of producing inconsistent runtime behavior.

behavior: Pytest now creates a temporary unittest.TestCase instance with the method name runTest during collection and fixture discovery.
Collected unittest test items now expose their callable as a bound method on a TestCase instance instead of an unbound class function.
Function-scoped fixture requests for unittest-style tests resolve against the active TestCase instance, while non-function scopes do not expose an instance.
Method fixtures are bound through the standard instance-binding path, so unittest fixture handling is aligned with other class-based pytest tests.
Custom TestCase constructors that assume the requested method already exists for every method name can now fail during collection when pytest passes runTest.
Async unittest test methods continue to be executed through the unittest runner using the bound test instance.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest collects a unittest.TestCase subclass, it should be able to create a temporary instance using runTest for discovery without crashing if the class is compatible with standard unittest construction.
When a unittest-based test item is inspected during collection or execution, its callable should behave as a bound method of a TestCase instance rather than as an unbound function on the class.
When a function-scoped fixture is resolved for a unittest-style test, it should receive the current TestCase instance as the request instance context.
When a fixture is resolved outside function scope, it should not expose a per-test TestCase instance.
When a custom TestCase subclass overrides __init__ and does not tolerate runTest, pytest should fail during collection instead of proceeding with inconsistent discovery.
When an async unittest test method is executed, pytest should still delegate execution through unittest using the instantiated test case.

task_5.title: Surface unittest class cleanup failures in pytest
task_5.description: Pytest 8.2.0 fixes its unittest integration so exceptions raised by class cleanup callbacks registered with TestCase.addClassCleanup() are reported during class setup or teardown instead of being silently ignored. When several class cleanup callbacks fail, their failures are surfaced together rather than dropping all but one or passing unexpectedly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that unittest-based tests run through pytest report failures from class cleanup callbacks registered with TestCase.addClassCleanup() instead of completing without surfacing those errors.

expectation.grounded: For unittest.TestCase classes executed by pytest, errors captured during doClassCleanups() after callbacks registered with TestCase.addClassCleanup() run must be reported as class-level failures. If exactly one class cleanup exception exists, pytest should report that exception directly. If multiple class cleanup exceptions exist, pytest should report them as an ExceptionGroup-style aggregated error. This reporting must also occur when class cleanup runs after a setUpClass() or tearDownClass() failure.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should treat unittest class cleanup failures as real execution errors. A single cleanup failure should appear as that failure, and multiple cleanup failures should appear together as one grouped cleanup error, including when cleanup happens after another class lifecycle error.

constraints.grounded: Pytest must not silently suppress exceptions raised by addClassCleanup() callbacks. It must continue to execute class cleanups on both the normal teardown path and the path where class setup raises, while preserving the underlying cleanup exceptions in the reported outcome. A lone cleanup exception should remain ungrouped for readable reporting, and multiple cleanup exceptions should preserve all member failures.
constraints.conceptual: Class cleanup behavior should remain intact, but cleanup failures can no longer disappear. Reporting should stay readable for one cleanup error and complete for several cleanup errors, without changing outcomes when no cleanup callback fails.

behavior: Pytest now inspects unittest class cleanup exceptions after class cleanups have been executed.
A failure raised by a single TestCase.addClassCleanup() callback is surfaced directly as the reported class cleanup error.
Failures raised by multiple TestCase.addClassCleanup() callbacks are surfaced together as one grouped cleanup error instead of being silently lost.
Class cleanup failures are reported even if they occur while pytest is already handling a setUpClass() or tearDownClass() failure.
When no class cleanup callback fails, existing unittest class setup and teardown behavior is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a unittest.TestCase executed by pytest registers one addClassCleanup() callback and that callback raises, pytest should report an error caused by class cleanup instead of finishing without that error.
When a unittest.TestCase executed by pytest registers multiple addClassCleanup() callbacks and more than one raises, pytest should report one grouped cleanup error containing all cleanup failures.
When setUpClass() fails after registering addClassCleanup() callbacks that also raise, pytest should still run the registered class cleanups and surface the cleanup failure information.
When tearDownClass() or normal class teardown completes and registered addClassCleanup() callbacks raise, pytest should expose those cleanup failures as teardown-related errors.
When addClassCleanup() callbacks do not raise, pytest should preserve the prior observable outcome of the unittest-based test class.

task_6.title: Preserve full short summary output at -vv
task_6.description: The upgrade fixes pytest terminal reporting so the `short test summary info` section no longer truncates long failure text when tests are run with `-vv`. This aligns high-verbosity local runs with the existing full-message behavior seen on CI while preserving trimmed output at lower verbosity.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the `short test summary info` section shows the complete failure summary text for each failed test when pytest is run with `-vv`, so users can inspect long assertion details directly from the summary instead of seeing a width-trimmed version.

expectation.grounded: When pytest renders a failed test line in `short test summary info`, the failure message appended to that line should not be width-trimmed if the session is running with verbosity level 2 or higher (`-vv`). At lower verbosity, the summary line should continue to be trimmed to available terminal width unless the run is detected as CI, where the full message remains shown.
expectation.conceptual: High-verbosity runs should expose the full failure summary in the short summary section. Standard local runs should keep the compact, truncated summary format, while environments that already show full output should continue to do so.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to how the summary line message is formatted in `short test summary info`. It must not alter which tests appear in the summary, the failure classification, or the existing compact formatting behavior for non-CI runs below `-vv`. CI behavior that already avoids truncation must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Only the visibility of long summary text should change. Existing summary membership, failure reporting semantics, and lower-verbosity compact output should remain stable.

behavior: Failed entries in `short test summary info` include the full failure message when pytest is invoked with `-vv` or higher verbosity.
At default verbosity and with `-v`, long failure messages in `short test summary info` continue to be shortened to fit the available line width during non-CI runs.
CI runs continue to show the full short-summary failure message regardless of local terminal width trimming rules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a failed test with a long assertion explanation, when pytest is run with `-vv`, then the corresponding `short test summary info` line should include the full failure message rather than a width-trimmed form.

Given the same failed test, when pytest is run without `-vv` in a non-CI environment, then the `short test summary info` line should remain compact and may truncate long failure text to fit the terminal width.
When pytest is run in a CI environment, the `short test summary info` line should continue to include the full failure message even if it would otherwise exceed the available display width.

task_4.title: Adopt pytest 8.2 importorskip warning semantics
task_4.description: Pytest 8.2.0 expands `pytest.importorskip()` so callers can choose which import exception should trigger a skip. The default behavior now surfaces broken or partially installed optional dependencies by warning when a module is found but import fails with `ImportError`, while still allowing callers to opt into the previous skip behavior explicitly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.importorskip()` distinguishes between a dependency that is missing and one that is present but fails during import, and allow callers to explicitly control which `ImportError` subtype should be treated as a skip condition instead of always silently skipping import failures.

expectation.grounded: `pytest.importorskip()` should accept a keyword-only `exc_type` parameter whose public contract is `ImportError` or one of its subclasses. When `exc_type` is not provided, `pytest.importorskip()` should continue to skip on `ImportError`, but if the caught exception is not `ModuleNotFoundError` it should also emit a `PytestDeprecationWarning`. When `exc_type=ImportError` is passed explicitly, the function should skip on `ImportError` without emitting that warning. If a narrower exception type such as `ModuleNotFoundError` is supplied, only that exception type should be converted into a skip and other import-time failures should propagate normally. Successful imports should still return the imported module.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare which import failure is considered an acceptable reason to skip. Missing optional dependencies should still skip cleanly, but dependencies that exist and fail to import for installation or environment reasons should no longer be silently treated the same way by default; callers must opt in if they still want that behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable behavior for successful imports, explicit skip reasons, or existing version-based acceptance after a module is imported. The new warning should only appear when the default handling catches an `ImportError` that is not a `ModuleNotFoundError`, and explicit `exc_type=ImportError` should suppress that warning while preserving skip behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Keep ordinary optional-dependency skips working as before, and limit the new warning to cases that indicate a dependency was found but is broken or incompletely installed rather than simply absent.

behavior: `pytest.importorskip()` accepts an optional keyword-only `exc_type` argument to define which `ImportError` subclass is converted into a skip outcome.
When `pytest.importorskip()` is called without `exc_type` and the target module is missing, it skips without issuing a warning because the failure is a `ModuleNotFoundError`.
When `pytest.importorskip()` is called without `exc_type` and the target module exists but raises another `ImportError` during import, it still skips but also emits a `PytestDeprecationWarning`.
When `pytest.importorskip()` is called with `exc_type=ImportError`, import failures raising `ImportError` continue to produce a skip without the deprecation warning.
When `pytest.importorskip()` is called with a narrower `exc_type`, only failures of that type are converted to skips; other import-time exceptions are not swallowed by `importorskip()`.
If the module imports successfully, `pytest.importorskip()` continues to return the module object and preserve its normal post-import behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When an optional module is not installed and `pytest.importorskip()` is called with default arguments, it should skip execution without emitting a deprecation warning.

When a module is present but raises `ImportError` during import and `pytest.importorskip()` is called with default arguments, it should skip execution and emit a deprecation warning indicating that this default behavior is changing.
When a module is present but raises `ImportError` during import and `pytest.importorskip(..., exc_type=ImportError)` is used, it should skip execution without emitting that deprecation warning.

When `pytest.importorskip()` is configured with a narrower exception type such as `ModuleNotFoundError`, only that exception type should produce a skip and a different import-time `ImportError` should remain visible to the caller.
When a module imports successfully, `pytest.importorskip()` should return the imported module and continue to honor any existing version checks.

task_8.title: Expose pytest session version through PYTEST_VERSION
task_8.description: Pytest 8.2.0 introduces a built-in environment variable that exposes the active pytest version for the lifetime of a pytest run. This gives application and configuration code an early, standard way to detect that pytest is running, while ensuring the environment is restored after the run completes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure code that needs to change behavior during a pytest run can reliably detect that pytest is active by reading a standard environment variable, without depending on late fixture setup or external plugins.

expectation.grounded: During a pytest invocation, the process environment should contain `PYTEST_VERSION` with the same value as `pytest.__version__`. The variable should be set before pytest finishes preparing configuration so early startup and configuration code can observe it, and it should be cleaned up when the invocation ends.
expectation.conceptual: A pytest run should provide a built-in environment signal that indicates pytest is currently running and identifies the active pytest version. That signal should be available early in startup and should no longer be present once the run is over.

constraints.grounded: If `PYTEST_VERSION` already exists before pytest starts, pytest should temporarily override it during the run and restore the original value afterward. If it did not exist beforehand, pytest should not leave the variable defined after completion.
constraints.conceptual: The detection mechanism should be session-scoped and non-destructive: it may affect the environment while pytest is active, but it must not permanently change the caller's environment after execution finishes.

behavior: Pytest sets `PYTEST_VERSION` in the process environment for the duration of a pytest invocation.
The value exposed through `PYTEST_VERSION` matches `pytest.__version__`.
The variable is available during early pytest startup, including configuration-time code that runs before the session is fully prepared.
If the environment already contained `PYTEST_VERSION`, pytest restores that original value when the invocation exits.
If no prior `PYTEST_VERSION` value existed, pytest removes the variable when the invocation exits.
acceptance_criteria: When a process is running under pytest 8.2.0, reading `PYTEST_VERSION` during pytest startup or test execution should report the same version string as `pytest.__version__`.
When application or configuration code executes as part of pytest startup, it should be able to use `PYTEST_VERSION` to determine that the current process is inside a pytest run.
When pytest finishes and `PYTEST_VERSION` was not set before the invocation, the environment should no longer contain `PYTEST_VERSION`.
When pytest finishes and `PYTEST_VERSION` had a pre-existing value before the invocation, that original value should be restored.

task_7.title: Improve namespace package detection for importlib collection
task_7.description: The update fixes namespace-package discovery when namespace handling is enabled so importlib-based collection resolves module names from the same package root Python can actually import, including editable-install layouts that were missed before. This prevents incorrect module-name resolution that could surface as collection-time import failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that namespace-package projects are discovered and imported correctly when namespace package handling is enabled, including layouts where the package is importable through normal Python resolution but not identifiable solely by direct `sys.path` ancestry.

expectation.grounded: When `consider_namespace_packages` is enabled, pytest should resolve a module's package root by checking upward candidate roots and selecting one only when the computed fully qualified module name is importable through normal Python import resolution and maps back to the same module path. This should improve collection and import behavior for namespace-package layouts such as editable installs, while preserving the existing failure mode for paths that still cannot be resolved to a package/module name.
expectation.conceptual: Enabling namespace-package support should make pytest recognize more valid namespace-package layouts and import them the way Python would, instead of misclassifying them and failing during collection.

constraints.grounded: Namespace-package detection must not promote a candidate root unless the resolved module name is actually importable and corresponds to the target file. If no valid package or namespace-package root can be confirmed, resolution should still fail rather than inventing an incorrect module name.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should be permissive for real namespace packages but conservative about ambiguous paths: it should accept valid importable layouts and reject paths that do not truly belong to an importable package structure.

behavior: With `consider_namespace_packages` enabled, package-root resolution should evaluate upward directory candidates using the module name implied by each candidate root rather than relying only on whether a parent directory is literally present on `sys.path`.
A namespace-package root should be accepted only if Python can normally resolve the computed module name and that resolution points to the same module file being collected.
Namespace-package layouts reachable through mechanisms such as editable installs should resolve successfully when their modules are importable under normal Python rules.
Paths that do not correspond to an importable package or namespace package should continue to fail package-root resolution instead of producing an incorrect import target.
acceptance_criteria: When a test or module belongs to a namespace package and `consider_namespace_packages` is enabled, pytest should derive the fully qualified module name that normal Python importing would use for that file.

When the namespace package is available through an editable install or another import mechanism that does not depend on a parent directory being directly listed on `sys.path`, collection should still succeed if Python can import that module normally.
When an upward directory candidate would yield a module name that Python cannot import for the target file, pytest should not treat that candidate as the package root.
When a file does not belong to any resolvable package or namespace package, pytest should continue to fail resolution rather than collecting it under an incorrect module name.

task_9.title: Restore per-test instances for class, static, and classmethod tests
task_9.description: Pytest 8.2.0 fixes a regression affecting class-based tests declared with @staticmethod or @classmethod. These tests now receive a fresh per-test class instance like regular test methods, so setup_method and instance-bound fixtures work consistently and no longer fail or share instance state unexpectedly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest test classes using `setup_method` continue to work when individual tests are declared with `@staticmethod` or `@classmethod`, and that those tests use isolated per-test instance state instead of running without an instance or reusing shared `self` state.

expectation.grounded: For tests collected from a pytest class, `request.instance` should return a fresh class instance during function-scoped execution not only for regular instance methods, but also for tests declared with `@staticmethod` and `@classmethod`. `setup_method` and fixture methods defined on the class should execute against that instance for those tests, so they no longer fail because the instance is missing and they no longer share a single class instance across fixture usage. Outside function scope, `request.instance` should remain `None`.
expectation.conceptual: Static and class method tests inside a test class should behave like normal test methods for setup and fixture handling. Each collected test should run with its own class instance, exposing that instance where pytest normally provides one, while broader-scoped or non-class executions should not gain a synthetic instance.

constraints.grounded: Do not change standalone function behavior: tests that are not methods of a collected test class should still have no class instance. Keep `request.instance` unavailable for non-function-scoped requests. Preserve correct fixture binding by only binding class fixture methods to the active test instance when the fixture logically belongs to that class context.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the new instance behavior to per-test class executions. Module-level tests and broader-scoped fixture contexts should continue to behave as before, and fixture binding should remain consistent with the object that owns the fixture.

behavior: `request.instance` is populated for function-scoped execution of tests collected from a pytest class, including tests declared with `@staticmethod` and `@classmethod`.
Each collected test method in a class receives its own fresh class instance, rather than sharing one instance across multiple tests or fixture invocations.
A class-level `setup_method` can run successfully for staticmethod and classmethod tests because an instance is available during method setup.
Fixture methods declared on the test class, including autouse fixtures, are resolved against the active per-test instance for staticmethod and classmethod tests.
`request.instance` remains `None` for non-function-scoped requests and for tests that are not methods on a collected pytest class.
acceptance_criteria: When a pytest test class defines `setup_method` and includes a `@staticmethod` test, running that test should not fail because of a missing instance, and `request.instance` should reference a fresh instance for that test.

When a pytest test class defines `setup_method` and includes a `@classmethod` test, running that test should not fail because of a missing instance, and `request.instance` should reference a fresh instance for that test.

When fixture methods are declared on a pytest test class and used by regular, static, or class method tests, each collected test should observe fixture state on its own instance rather than sharing mutable instance state through a reused `self`.
When `request.instance` is accessed from a standalone test function or from a non-function-scoped fixture request, it should be `None`.

task_11.title: Preserve package submodule access in pytest importlib mode
task_11.description: Pytest 8.2.0 fixes importlib-based collection so nested modules remain accessible through their parent packages during doctest and test collection, and module resolution stays tied to the requested file path instead of a same-named unrelated import target.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.2.0 restores standard Python package behavior when using importlib-based collection, especially with doctest collection enabled, so imported submodules remain available through their parent modules and collection does not fail because expected parent attributes are missing.

expectation.grounded: When pytest runs with `--import-mode=importlib`, including alongside `--doctest-modules`, importing a module or package such as `foo.bar` or `foo.bar.baz` must also make the imported child available as an attribute on its parent module, matching normal Python import behavior. `import_path(..., mode=ImportMode.importlib)` should reuse the cached module object for repeated imports, import missing parent packages as needed, and only use a discovered `ModuleSpec` when its origin matches the requested module path so the resolved module comes from the intended file or package.
expectation.conceptual: In importlib-based pytest collection, package imports should behave like normal Python imports: parent packages should expose imported children, repeated imports should remain stable, and pytest should load the requested module from the correct location. Enabling doctest collection should no longer break code that accesses submodules through their parent packages.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress working `--import-mode=importlib` imports for regular packages, modules, or namespace-package layouts. Preserve module identity through the import cache, avoid parent-child links that point at the wrong module object, and avoid resolving a target module from a spec whose origin does not equal the requested path.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should restore expected import behavior without changing which modules users asked pytest to collect. It must not create duplicate module instances, incorrect parent-child links, or accidental resolution to similarly named modules elsewhere on the import path.

behavior: Importlib-mode collection imports parent modules as needed before loading a child module.
After a child module or package is imported, its parent module exposes that child as an attribute, enabling parent.child and deeper attribute access during collection and doctest execution.
Repeated importlib-mode imports of the same module continue to return the already loaded module object instead of a new instance.

When resolving a module through finder hooks, pytest only uses a spec if its origin matches the requested module path, preventing unrelated same-named modules or namespace packages from being treated as the target import.
When pytest synthesizes missing intermediate modules in importlib mode, parent modules still retain attribute links to their loaded child modules.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package tree with nested modules, when pytest collects it with `--import-mode=importlib`, then each imported parent module should expose the collected child module as an attribute.

Given `--import-mode=importlib` and `--doctest-modules`, when code imports a submodule and later accesses it through its parent package, then collection should succeed without an `AttributeError` caused by a missing parent attribute.

Given the same module is imported multiple times through pytest's importlib path, when it has already been loaded, then pytest should return the existing module instance rather than creating a second one.

Given a same-named directory or namespace candidate elsewhere on `sys.path`, when pytest imports a specific module path in importlib mode, then the loaded module should come from the requested file path instead of the unrelated location.

task_10.title: Stabilize pytest fixture caching and teardown ordering
task_10.description: The upgrade adopts corrected fixture lifecycle behavior in pytest so cached scoped fixtures do not repeatedly attach teardown callbacks to their dependencies, teardown order remains consistent when dependent fixtures are reused, unparametrized scoped fixtures reuse a stable cache entry, and fixture cleanup still runs when setup fails after registering finalizers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that repeated access to cached fixtures does not duplicate teardown registration, alter the expected reverse teardown order of dependent fixtures, or cause inconsistent reuse and cleanup behavior for scoped fixtures.

expectation.grounded: For pytest fixtures declared with `@pytest.fixture`, retrieving a fixture value from cache must not re-add that fixture's finalizer to requested parent fixtures. Scoped fixtures that depend on other fixtures must still be invalidated correctly when a parametrized dependency changes, but otherwise should reuse their cached value or cached exception across requests in the same scope. Fixtures without a direct parameter value should use a stable cache identity rather than a per-request index. If fixture setup raises after registering finalizers, teardown for that fixture should still be scheduled so registered cleanup executes once.
expectation.conceptual: Cached fixture reuse should be side-effect free: asking for the same scoped fixture again should not change teardown ordering or queue extra cleanup. Shared scoped fixtures should behave like a single cached instance within their scope, including consistent reuse of setup failures, while still cleaning up correctly when setup does not complete successfully.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress dependency invalidation for fixtures that rely on parametrized fixtures. Do not register teardown against the synthetic `request` fixture. Do not cause scoped fixtures to execute setup or teardown more times than their cache lifecycle requires, including when a cached failure is reused.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing dependency invalidation rules and fixture semantics while eliminating duplicate cleanup scheduling. The change should only remove unintended extra teardown or cache churn, not alter legitimate fixture lifetime boundaries.

behavior: When a fixture depends on other fixtures, pytest should resolve those dependencies before deciding whether the fixture can be served from cache, so dependency invalidation still takes effect.
If a fixture value is already cached, reusing it should not attach another teardown callback to its requested parent fixtures.
When multiple scoped fixtures share a parent fixture, re-requesting one cached child fixture should no longer make it tear down earlier than siblings that were set up later.
Fixtures without an explicit parameter value should share a stable cache key so repeated requests within the same scope reuse the same cached result or cached exception.
If fixture setup fails after registering finalizers, pytest should still schedule the fixture's own finalization so cleanup registered for that fixture can run during teardown.
acceptance_criteria: When a scoped fixture is requested more than once in the same scope and its value is already cached, it should not gain additional teardown registrations on any dependency fixture.

When two scoped child fixtures depend on the same parent fixture and one child is requested again later from cache, teardown should still occur in reverse order of setup rather than being reordered by the repeated access.
When an unparametrized scoped fixture is used by multiple tests in the same scope, pytest should reuse one cached outcome instead of treating each request as a distinct cache entry.

When a scoped fixture previously failed during setup and is requested again in the same scope, pytest should reuse the cached failure consistently instead of rerunning setup because of a request-index-only cache difference.
When fixture setup raises after registering cleanup, the registered cleanup should still run once when the owning node is finalized.

task_12.title: Correct Scoped Fixture Resolution And Teardown Ordering
task_12.description: Pytest 8.2.0 fixes fixture lifecycle handling so scoped fixture dependencies are resolved through the standard fixture request path and finalized in a stable reverse-setup order. This prevents incorrect teardown ordering and duplicate cleanup when fixtures are autouse, requested dynamically, reused from cache, depend on parametrized fixtures, or fail during setup.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that fixture dependencies behave consistently across explicit, autouse, and dynamically requested usage so scoped fixtures are set up once per cache key, finalized exactly once, and torn down in reverse order of initialization even when later tests reuse only part of the dependency graph or a fixture setup fails.

expectation.grounded: Fixture dependency resolution should go through the normal `FixtureRequest` path, including `request.getfixturevalue` and legacy dynamic fixture access patterns, so scope validation and fixture lookup rules are applied uniformly. For scoped fixtures, `FixtureDef.execute` should return cached values or cached setup exceptions without re-registering finalizers, should register dependent finalization so child fixtures finish before parent fixtures, and should still schedule fixture cleanup on the node even if fixture setup raises. Invalid cross-scope access must continue to raise `ScopeMismatch`, and fixture lookup or unsupported parametrized-fixture access without a parameter must still fail rather than silently reusing a fixture.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, fixture dependencies should resolve the same way whether they are listed directly, provided automatically, or requested dynamically at runtime. Reusing a scoped fixture should not cause repeated setup or repeated teardown, teardown should always unwind from the most recently initialized dependency back to its parents, and cleanup should still occur if fixture setup aborts. Scope and lookup errors should remain enforced consistently.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public contract that fixture lookup failures raise `FixtureLookupError`, invalid higher-scope to lower-scope access raises `ScopeMismatch`, and requesting a parametrized fixture without an available parameter is rejected. Cached fixture reuse must not enqueue extra finalizers, and teardown ordering must remain dependency-aware for autouse fixtures, dynamically requested fixtures, and fixtures that depend on parametrized fixtures.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve existing error conditions and safety checks while removing duplicate cleanup and out-of-order teardown. It must not make fixture reuse or dynamic fixture access bypass scope rules, and it must not introduce extra setup or teardown cycles for the same scoped fixture instance.

behavior: Fixtures requested as dependencies are resolved through the standard fixture request API instead of by directly consuming cached dependency values.
Scoped fixture teardown now preserves reverse initialization order even when the dependency was introduced through autouse behavior or dynamic fixture access.
When a scoped fixture value is reused from cache, its finalizer is not re-registered, preventing duplicate teardown or incorrect teardown ordering.

If a fixture depends on another fixture that is invalidated or finalized because of parametrization changes, the dependent fixture is finalized before the parent fixture and can be recomputed cleanly.
If fixture setup raises after registering cleanup, the fixture cleanup is still scheduled so finalization runs once.
Scope validation is applied consistently when resolving or reusing fixtures, including dynamically requested fixtures and already-cached fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: When two scoped fixtures are initialized in dependency order and a later test reuses only the parent fixture, teardown should still happen in strict reverse setup order, with the child fixture finalizing before the parent fixture.

When a fixture is made active through autouse behavior or `request.getfixturevalue` rather than only through a test function argument list, it should follow the same dependency ordering and teardown guarantees as an explicitly requested fixture.
When the same scoped fixture is requested multiple times within its scope, it should run setup once and teardown once for the cached fixture instance.
When a scoped fixture setup fails after adding cleanup, subsequent requests in the same scope should not accumulate duplicate finalizers, and the cleanup should still execute once.
When a fixture access violates scope rules, the request should raise `ScopeMismatch` instead of returning a cached fixture value.
When fixture lookup is invalid or a parametrized fixture is requested without an available parameter, the request should still fail with the existing fixture error behavior.

task_13.title: Require pluggy 1.5.0 or newer for pytest 8.2.0
task_13.description: Pytest 8.2.0 raises the minimum supported pluggy version to 1.5.0. Upgrading from 8.1.2 therefore requires dependency resolution and plugin-based usage to align with that newer compatibility baseline.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from pytest 8.1.2 to 8.2.0 also upgrades the supported runtime baseline to pluggy 1.5.0 or newer so installations and plugin-driven usage remain compatible.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.2.0 should require pluggy>=1.5.0 as part of its supported runtime contract. Users upgrading from 8.1.2 should treat environments resolving an older pluggy version as incompatible, and plugin integrations should run against the newer pluggy baseline.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should make a newer pluggy release part of the supported environment so the framework and its plugin ecosystem run on a consistent dependency baseline after moving to pytest 8.2.0.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer additional behavioral changes beyond the documented dependency floor. The observable upgrade requirement supported by the provided materials is the minimum supported pluggy version and the resulting compatibility boundary for environments and plugins.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the scope of the change limited to dependency compatibility and avoid implying unrelated behavior changes.

behavior: Upgrading to pytest 8.2.0 requires pluggy version 1.5.0 or later.
An environment that keeps pluggy below 1.5.0 is outside the supported configuration for pytest 8.2.0.
Plugin-based usage after the upgrade is expected to operate against the pluggy 1.5.0-or-newer baseline.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades to pytest 8.2.0, the resolved dependency set should include pluggy version 1.5.0 or newer.
When an environment provides pluggy below version 1.5.0, the upgraded pytest 8.2.0 configuration should be treated as incompatible rather than supported.
When pytest 8.2.0 is used with plugins in a supported environment, those plugins should run against the pluggy 1.5.0-or-newer baseline.

task_14.title: Make pytest cache initialization atomic
task_14.description: Pytest 8.2.0 changes cache initialization so the cache directory's supporting metadata is created together with the cache directory itself. This avoids partially initialized cache state where cache content can appear without the standard support files after an interrupted or competing first write.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest cache initialization creates a fully initialized cache directory in one step, so first-time cache use does not leave a partial cache state missing the standard support files.

expectation.grounded: When the cache provider first creates cache storage through public cache operations such as Cache.mkdir(name) or Cache.set(key, value), it should ensure the cache root is initialized together with its standard support files, including README.md, .gitignore, and CACHEDIR.TAG, before exposing child cache paths or values. Once the cache root already exists, these operations should reuse it rather than recreating or overwriting the existing support files.
expectation.conceptual: Any first use of pytest's cache should produce a complete, ready-to-use cache directory rather than exposing a half-created directory. Existing cache directories should continue to work as-is without having their metadata rewritten.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing cache provider APIs and normal cache layout while tightening initialization semantics only. Do not require callers to change how they create cache values or cache subdirectories, and do not overwrite support files for an already existing cache directory.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve cache-directory consistency without changing how users interact with the cache feature or replacing metadata that is already present.

behavior: First-time cache initialization now creates the cache root and its support files as a single observable operation instead of creating the cache root first and filling in support files afterward.
The standard cache support files are created together when the cache root is first initialized, rather than being added later on demand.
Creating a named cache directory now triggers the same cache-root initialization guarantees as writing a cached value.
Subsequent cache operations against an already existing cache directory reuse the existing directory and leave any existing support files unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest first creates cache state through a cache value write, it should create a fully initialized cache directory with the standard support files already present before the cached value is exposed.
When pytest first creates cache state through cache directory creation, it should provide the same fully initialized cache directory semantics.
When cache initialization is observed during first-time creation, it should not expose a cache directory that contains cache content while one or more standard support files are missing.
When the cache directory already exists, later cache operations should succeed without recreating or overwriting the existing support files.
